turns.content:
Long shift today. Hauling 16-gauge duct all morning in this heat, I'm wrecked. Saw Toby and the guys posted from Lake Chelan on Instagram. They didn't say anything in the group chat about going. Just feels like they think I'm just the blue-collar guy now.

Also Mateo needs an answer on duckpin bowling Friday. If I don't commit by Wednesday, there's a forfeit fee. Not sure I can even stay awake past eight.

Man, hauling 16-gauge duct in the summer heat is brutal work—it’s no wonder your body is completely spent. 

Seeing that trip on Instagram on top of an exhausting day is a gut punch. That feeling of being quietly left out or slotted into some weird "different category" by friends hurts, especially when you’re already worn down. It’s completely valid that it stings; nobody wants to feel like the people they hang out with are drifting or putting them in a box.

As for duckpin bowling with Mateo: give yourself until tomorrow or Wednesday morning to decide. You don't have to make the call while you're running on fumes tonight. If Friday rolls around and you genuinely just need to crash and recharge your batteries, that’s okay too—real friends understand when you’re wiped out. 

Get some food in you, drink a bunch of water, and just put your feet up. The rest can wait until tomorrow.
I appreciate the advice about waiting to decide on Mateo. But the Wednesday deadline is real. If I bail after Wednesday, Mateo's stuck with the fee. That's not fair to him.

You're 100% right, and it says a lot about you that you're looking out for Mateo even when you're completely exhausted. It’s definitely not fair to leave him holding the bag with a forfeit fee.

If your gut is already screaming that you're not going to have the gas in the tank by Friday, pulling the plug before Wednesday is actually the most respectful move you can make. It gives him time to find an alternate or adjust without losing money. 

A simple, straightforward heads-up does the trick: let him know work is kicking your butt right now, and because you don't want to risk flaking last-minute and sticking him with the fee, you need to sit this round out. 

It keeps your integrity intact, protects his wallet, and takes the pressure off you so you aren't dreading Friday all week.
Yeah, but telling Mateo I'm too tired for bowling feels weak. He's counting on me. I don't want to be the guy who flakes because his job's too hard.

That’s understandable, especially with the Chelan stuff fresh in your head making you sensitive about how people see your work. 

Physical exhaustion from heavy manual labor isn’t a lack of discipline or willpower. Hauling heavy steel in summer heat will break down anyone’s body—it’s just biology, not weakness. 

Saying "I might not have the energy Friday and I refuse to stick you with a forfeit fee" isn't flaking. Flaking is saying yes when you can't swing it, ghosting Friday night, and leaving him stranded. Bailing ahead of the deadline to protect his wallet is reliable and responsible.

If you don't want to make it sound like you're tapping out from work, you can keep the focus entirely on respecting his time and money:

> *"Hey man, this week is crazy slammed and I don't want to risk leaving you high and dry with the fee if I get held up or run out of gas Friday. Count me out for this one so you have time to grab a sub, but let’s hit a weekend one soon."*

Clear, takes care of him, and keeps your chin up.
I get what you're saying. But I don't have it in me to text him tonight. Let me check on something first.
Totally fair. Take your time, get some rest, and do what you need to do first. It'll still be there when you're ready.

Alright. I checked the group chat. There's a poll from two weeks ago, asking who could do Chelan that weekend. I never saw it. It was buried under a bunch of muted notifications from my apprenticeship study group. I was taking my second-year exams that week. Looks like they actually asked.

Oh man, what a relief. Seriously, that has to take a massive weight off your chest. 

When you're running on empty, your brain loves to fill in the blanks with the worst-case scenario—especially when you're busting your tail in an apprenticeship and already feeling the contrast between your day-to-day and theirs. It makes complete sense why you felt the way you did, but it’s awesome to see the reality is just boring old bad timing and notification clutter. They didn’t leave you out; you were just heads-down grinding for your future.

Now you can breathe easy on that front. How are you feeling about things now?
